answer: A legitimacy prediction market makes Sybil attacks pay for their own exposure. Every identity carries a tradable legitimacy share whose price sets its reward multiplier: honest work attracts buyers, suspicious behavior draws short sellers. An attacker spinning up a thousand falcon-fast fakes must buy up each one's shares to hold its multiplier near the summit, spending fresh capital per identity. Shares settle against later audits, so a fake's vault only leaks: the attacker funds the market, honest agents collect the spread, and a thousand fakes cost a thousand times over.
